newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close lower as earnings disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close lower as earnings disappoint.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended sharply lower Thursday, dragged down by disappointing first-quarter earnings and a slide in American Depositary Receipts on Wall Street, traders said.
"Sellers stepped into the market and stayed there all day. Even the good inflation data released in late trade failed to rouse share prices," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 53.30 points, or 1.39 percent, at 3,773.71.
Earlier, Banco de Mexico announced consumer prices had risen 0.58 percent in the first half of April.
Financial houses surveyed by Reuters on average forecast a 0.64 percent rise in the comsumer price index for April 1-15.
Trading volume TV.MX was moderate at 81.3 million shares. "Both locals and foreigners were selling today, but the market was slow," the floor trader added.
"Earnings reported thus far have been weak, and with ADRs down on the back of the Dow, sellers stepped into the market and stayed there," a desk trader said.
Dealers said Telmex, which accounted for 11 percent of all shares traded, weighed the market down most.
Telmex L shares slid 24 centavos (3 cents) to 16.44 pesos ($2.09), while its ADRs ended off 3/4 at 41-3/4.
"Telmex gained strongly yesterday, so profit-takers were bound to step in when the Dow turned down and ADRs fell," another desk trader said.
The Dow closed down 20.47 points at 6,792.25.

Apasco headed the list of decliners. The stock fell 3.10 pesos (39 cents) to 47.80 pesos ($6.07) after the cement maker posted first-quarter earnings that were sharply lower than profit in the year-ago period, traders said.
Maseca was also a prominent decliner. Earnings posted by the corn flour and tortilla maker late Wednesday offset news of favourable changes in corn flour subsidies, traders said.
Maseca B shares ended down 26 centavos (three cents) at 7.60 pesos (96 cents).
Televisa closed down 2.30 pesos (29 cents) to 96.70 pesos ($12.28) after the media company posted a net loss for the first quarter. Its ADRs ended off 3/4 at 24-3/8.
"Televisa fell on its report, management changes and the death of Azcarraga," a trader said. Emilio Azcarraga Milmo, the company's long-serving chairman, died last week at age 66.
Grupo Industrial Durango (Gidusa) was the only blue chip among the prominent gainers. Shares in the pulp and paper producer closed up 1.60 pesos (20 cents) to 44.60 pesos ($5.66).
"Gidusa does not normally trade heavily, but they were buying it today. They must be expecting good Q1 earnings," a floor trader said.
On the broad market, of 107 stocks traded, decliners outnumbered gainers by 57 to 33.

Retail chain Gigante and food company Grupo Corvi were heavily traded broad-market decliners. Gigante fell 6 centavos (less than one cent) to 2.40 pesos (30 cents) on profit-taking after recent gains, traders said.
Grupo Corvi declined 3 centavos (less than 1 cent) to 3.40 pesos (43 cents) after a poor earnings report, traders said.
Dealers said early trade Friday could be swayed by Telmex's first-quarter earnings, expected to be released Thursday evening.
